name_note: GTDB names this species Otoolea fessa; its genomes carry the NCBI name Clostridium fessum, the name under which it was described.

sentences.text: Clostridium fessum is an obligately anaerobic, Gram-positive, spore-forming bacterium isolated from the faeces of a healthy Korean subject.
Its cells are chained rods with tapered ends and it belongs to the family Lachnospiraceae, with Clostridium symbiosum the closest named species.
A later faecal isolate from a different study shared 94.7 percent 16S ribosomal RNA identity with it, among Lachnospiraceae relatives of Enterocloster.
A metagenomic study of newborn stool reported it as the predominant Clostridium species in both diseased and healthy specimens.
